profile.summary: RNA-MSM is an RNA language model that reads a multiple sequence alignment (MSA) of a target RNA and its homologues rather than a single sequence. It outputs a per-nucleotide embedding and attention maps, which the authors use to predict RNA secondary structure (base pairs) and solvent accessibility. The MSA must first be built with a homology search tool such as RNAcmap3.
profile.summary_source_locator: README.md: About The Project, Data Preparation; paper: Abstract

summary_quotes.text: RNA-MSM is the first unsupervised MSA RNA language model based on aligned homologous sequences that outputs both embedding and attention map to match different types of downstream tasks.
they can be directly mapped with high accuracy to 2D base pairing probabilities and 1D solvent accessibilities, respectively

we recommend utilizing our recently developed [RNAcmap3](https://academic.oup.com/gpb/article/22/1/qzae018/7617691) tool to search for homologous sequences of the target RNA sequences to serve as input for the RNA-MSM model

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: RNA-MSM follows the protein MSA Transformer design: an embedding module with two learned position embeddings, one for the rows (sequences in the MSA) and one for the columns (positions), then 10 transformer blocks with 12 attention heads each and a 768-dimensional embedding. The authors cut the block count from 12 to 10 because of GPU memory. It was trained with the BERT masked language modelling objective, masking 20% of MSA tokens. The 120 attention maps (10 blocks by 12 heads) and the embedding of the query sequence are the outputs; separate downstream networks in the repository turn them into secondary structure and solvent accessibility predictions.
sections.source_locator: paper: Materials and methods; Figure 1 legend; README.md: Inference; RNA_MSM_Inference.py

quotes.text: The embedding module consists of one initial embedding layer and two learnable position-embedding layers
The position-embedding layers encode rows (number of entries in the MSA) and columns (sequence length) of the MSA separately.
The RNA-MSM model is stacked with 10 transformer blocks, each containing 12 attention heads. The output embedding identifies all sequences in a 768-dimensional space.
The number of blocks was changed from 12 to 10 due to the graphics processing unit (GPU) memory limitation.
We employed the BERT masked language modeling objective function for training. Briefly, 20% tokens of the input MSA were substituted by a special token [MASK] at random.
A total of 120 attentional maps were constructed

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: One pretrained checkpoint is released on Google Drive (RNA_MSM_pretrained.ckpt by the script's default path). The repository also carries trained downstream models for secondary structure and solvent accessibility, and the downstream datasets with their MSAs were released in July 2024. Results depend strongly on the MSA, so a result should name the checkpoint, the repository commit, and the homology search tool and settings used to build the MSA.

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: MSA Transformer: 10 transformer blocks, 12 attention heads each, 768-dimensional embedding, with separate row and column position embeddings.

quotes.text: The RNA-MSM model is stacked with 10 transformer blocks, each containing 12 attention heads.

facts.label: Inputs
facts.value: An MSA of the target RNA and its homologues, as a file ending .a2m_msa2 in the results folder, listed by RNA ID in a text file.

quotes.text: The input MSA file should be be situated within `./results` folder, and its suffix ought to be `.a2m_msa2`.

facts.label: Outputs
facts.value: Attention maps of shape (seq_len, seq_len, 120) in *_atp.npy and an embedding of shape (seq_len, 768) in *_emb.npy. Downstream scripts write secondary structure (.ct, .bpseq, base-pair probability matrix) and solvent accessibility predictions.

strengths.text: Uses evolutionary information from homologous sequences, which the authors argue single-sequence BERT-style RNA models fail to capture.

quotes.text: they are ineffective at capturing the evolutionary information from homologous sequences

strengths.text: The authors chose validation and test sets structurally different from the training set, and excluded Rfam families with known structures from pretraining, to limit overlap.
strengths.source_locator: README.md: About The Project; paper: Materials and methods

quotes.text: choosing validation and test sets structurally different from the training set
Therefore, the RNAs used in downstream models would have no overlap with those used for training RNA-MSM.

strengths.text: Ready-made downstream predictors for secondary structure and solvent accessibility are included, and a free web server builds the MSA and runs both tasks.
strengths.source_locator: README.md: Downstream Prediction; Online RNA-MSM Sever

quotes.text: We also built a freely accessible [web server](https://aigene.cloudbastion.cn/#/rna-msm) for using the RNA-MSM models

limitations.text: Needs an MSA for every input. Building it requires a separate homology search (the authors recommend RNAcmap3), and prediction quality depends on the number and quality of homologues.

quotes.text: The effectiveness of predictions made by the RNA-MSM model is largely dependent on the quantity and quality of MSAs.

limitations.text: Sequence length is capped at 1024 positions in the inference script.
The environment pins old software (Python 3.8.5, PyTorch 1.7.1 with CUDA 11.0), and the inference script defaults to a CUDA device.
The script loads the checkpoint with torch.load on the path given as model_path, so that path must be the .ckpt file itself, while the README's command passes the pretrained folder.

run_guide.summary: Set up the RNA-MSM environment at a pinned commit, add the pretrained checkpoint, and extract embeddings and attention maps for the bundled example MSA.
prerequisites: conda, to build the environment from environment.yml (Python 3.8.5, PyTorch 1.7.1, CUDA toolkit 11.0).
A CUDA GPU by default; the script's device setting is cuda. Memory needs for inference are not stated.
A browser or other means to download the checkpoint from Google Drive. For new RNAs, an MSA built with RNAcmap3 or the web server.
Code is MIT. No licence is stated for the weights.
The README's clone command uses the SSH URL, which needs a GitHub SSH key; use the HTTPS URL otherwise.

steps.title: Get the code at the pinned commit
steps.shell:
git clone git@github.com:yikunpku/RNA-MSM.git
cd ./RNA-MSM
git checkout --detach faadd57559c1c146effbfd84a7628cd2042d5ede
steps.explanation: Clone and enter the repository as the README says (the README uses the SSH URL). The checkout line is added to pin the commit this page was read from.

steps.title: Create and activate the environment
steps.shell:
conda env create -f environment.yml
conda activate RNA-MSM
steps.explanation: Builds the conda environment. environment.yml names the environment rnamsm, so activation may need conda activate rnamsm instead of the README's RNA-MSM.
steps.source_locator: README.md: Create Environment with Anaconda; environment.yml

steps.title: Place the pretrained checkpoint
steps.explanation: Download the .ckpt file by hand from the README's Google Drive link and place it in ./pretrained. The script's default path is pretrained/RNA_MSM_pretrained.ckpt. The mkdir line is added.
steps.source_locator: README.md: Access Pre-trained Model; RNA_MSM_Inference.py: DataConfig

quotes.text: place the .ckpt files into the `./pretrained` folder

steps.title: Extract embedding and attention maps
steps.shell:
python RNA_MSM_Inference.py \
data.root_path=./ \
data.MSA_path=./results \
data.model_path=./pretrained \
data.MSA_list=rna_id.txt
steps.explanation: The README command. The repository ships rna_id.txt and an example MSA, results/2DRB_1.a2m_msa2.

quotes.text: python RNA_MSM_Inference.py \ data.root_path=./ \ data.MSA_path=./results \ data.model_path=./pretrained \ data.MSA_list=rna_id.txt

steps.title: Predict secondary structure
steps.explanation: The README's secondary structure command. --featdir must point to the folder holding the features from the previous step; the README writes ./results.
steps.source_locator: README.md: Downstream Prediction - RNA Secondary Structure (SS)

outputs: 2DRB_1_atp.npy (attention maps, seq_len by seq_len by 120) and 2DRB_1_emb.npy (embedding, seq_len by 768) in ./results; then SS_result/2DRB_1.ct, 2DRB_1.bpseq and 2DRB_1.prob.
limitations: These commands were read from the repository and have not been executed by Rewire.
The checkpoint must be downloaded by hand from Google Drive.
The README's activation name and the environment file's name differ (RNA-MSM against rnamsm).
Inputs for new RNAs need an MSA built outside this repository.
The README passes a folder as data.model_path while the script loads that path as a file; the .ckpt path may have to be given in full.

notes: The paper is CC BY-NC 4.0, so store_bytes is false for it; that is the article's licence, not a licence for the code or weights. The README's solvent accessibility command repeats 'python predict.py \' twice; it was left out of the run guide. The script passes data.model_path straight to torch.load, so the README's folder path may need to be the .ckpt file instead.
